authority.alpha_prerequisite: Make the D-01-installed RRFlow process a concrete Connectome development target by proving one committed rrflowDB value survives abrupt process loss, service restart, fresh discovery, fresh authentication, and a public SDK query, then give the separate Connectome repository an exact source-audited implementation handoff that cannot mistake mocks, renamed SurrealDB code, hard-coded rows, or an unauthenticated health probe for a working RRFlow product.

current_behavior: At clean RRFlow baseline 3fa90fad, the primary rrflow binary plans/applies an installation, serves one installed RrdEngine, authenticates readiness, commits a claim through the public Rust client, and queries it in the first process. The test then kills that process and proves only offline structural verification; it never restarts serve, creates a fresh session, or queries the value again. The separate Connectome checkout at 38f68ce7 contains a useful but handwritten native RRD session prototype that is not invoked by any screen. Its active runtime screen declares RRD connected and every stage verified after only three unauthenticated GETs; its browser smoke test intercepts those GETs and returns fixed 0.1.0/local_daemon/rrd-lsm data. The checkout also retains SurrealDB packages renamed as RRFlow, an incompatible legacy rrflow start command, a hard-coded cloud endpoint and namespace/database, static attunement/automation truth, and client-invented diagnostics/control protocols. RRFlow has no concise guide that tells that repository exactly what to retain, remove, generate, wire, and prove against real persistence.
target_behavior: The primary installed-lifecycle test starts the same installed rrflow binary again after an abrupt kill, verifies the announced instance, repeats authenticated readiness, creates a new public-client session, executes the same bounded rrflowQL query, and proves the same committed claim identity/value at or beyond the acknowledged sequence before final offline verification. One supporting Connectome implementation guide binds its audit to the exact separate-checkout revision; identifies real, dead, mocked, hard-coded, parallel-authority, and legacy paths; specifies the target renderer-to-native-to-public-RRD-to-RrdEngine-to-rrflowKV boundary; gives exact RRFlow install/serve/ready commands and generated-contract inputs; defines the first file/symbol edit packages and stop conditions; and requires a real artifact test that commits, renders engine-issued coordinates, kills RRFlow, restarts, reconnects, and renders the same value. The guide clearly marks secure installed credential handoff, packaged generated SDK consumption, complete WebSocket dispatch, signed bundles, and full H-06 conformance as open rather than inventing an insecure workaround.
unchanged_behavior: README, objective, roadmap, and POA&M retain identity, outcome, dependency/status, and deficiency authority; no gate or deficiency closes.

Fjall remains only a pinned correctness/performance opponent. SurrealDB, Qdrant, Tauri, Connectome, and other external projects never become RRFlow persistence, lifecycle, query, or semantic authority.
The rrflow command tree remains version, install, serve, ready, and verify; this package adds no hidden operator command, credential broker, browser-authentication profile, or second lifecycle.
The executable operation catalogue, OpenAPI document, internal client bindings, and generated SDK projections remain the only permitted public-surface source; the guide adds no handwritten catalogue.
The Connectome sibling checkout is inspected read-only and is not edited, committed, pushed, imported, or made a build/runtime dependency of RRFlow in this package.
The test-only distribution override and engine-internal installed credential reader remain test fixtures and are not presented as production Connectome APIs.
A UI render, build, fake server, intercepted request, liveness/readiness response, open port, or static label remains non-qualifying evidence.
Version 1.0.0, protocol version 1, Cargo.lock, dependencies, official promotion target, and pre-release status do not change.

sources.title: Connectome authenticated native RRD client baseline
sources.retained_behavior: Retain loopback validation, redirect denial, response bounds, native credential/session ownership intent, correlation checks, and explicit close.
sources.rejected_assumption: A handwritten partial client, fake TCP server, or registered but unused Tauri commands prove that the product UI authenticates or persists through RRFlow.

sources.title: Tauri v2 calling Rust from the frontend
sources.retained_behavior: Use a narrow native command boundary for request/response and channels for ordered streaming; use raw bytes only where measured payloads justify them.
sources.rejected_assumption: Generic events, arbitrary commands, or JSON Value forwarding are an ordered high-throughput protocol, schema validator, or authorization boundary.

sources.title: OWASP HTML5 Security Cheat Sheet
sources.retained_behavior: Keep long-lived credentials out of browser storage and treat client-side data as untrusted input.
sources.rejected_assumption: A desktop webview makes connection profiles, localStorage, routes, logs, or serializable renderer state safe for operator credentials.

sources.rejected_assumption: Generated types alone prove runtime validation, authentication, transport safety, operation coverage, or persistence.
